integrity: The proof reduces Pearson X-squared exactly to a pair-collision count and conditions one pair on equality versus inequality. This yields the discrete-second-difference identity without approximation. Direct multinomial enumeration independently checks the likelihood-ratio specialization and representative power-divergence parameters.
scientific_limitations: The exact curvature identity assumes an equiprobable multinomial null.
The power-divergence positivity statement is restricted to lambda greater than -1; the modified likelihood statistic at lambda=-1 can diverge on empty cells.
The theorem is a covariance result and does not assert stochastic ordering or identical finite rejection regions.

An equivalent identity in older categorical-data literature remains the main originality risk because the complete 1984 foundational article was not available from a stable public full-text endpoint during source inspection.
title: Pearson covariance is exactly a binomial average of discrete curvature
